content:
To manage your personal settings, you must log into your Jira site. Public and anonymous users inherit the site's default user preferences.
Your personal settings let you customize some elements of Jira to your liking, including language, timezone, watch settings, and email type. For other settings, like your full name, avatar, password, and email address, see Managing your user profile.
To access your personal settings:
- From the top right of your screen, select Settings ().
- Under Personal Jira settings, select General settings.
You can update the following settings:
- Language – Change your Jira app language to one of the available options.
- Your timezone – The timezone used for date and time information across your Jira apps. If the timezone you select doesn't match your computer's timezone, you'll have the option to automatically update this preference.
- Watch your work items – With this enabled, you become a watcher of any work item that you create or comment on. This means you'll get an email when someone updates or comments on the work item.
Rovo can help you get to the right settings to make the changes you need. Open Rovo Chat and enter /find-jira-settings, then tell Rovo what you’re looking for. Rovo will provide a link to the most relevant settings page, along with a rundown on what you can do once you get there.
Manage notifications
To access your notification settings:
- From the top right of your screen, select Settings ().
- Under Personal Jira settings, select Notification settings.
You can choose what notifications you’d like to receive from a variety of work item activity.
You can choose to receive (or not receive) notifications in-app or by email by using the checkboxes.
Use the Customize space notifications section to set specific notifications for different spaces. You can customize notifications for up to 50 spaces.
All your notification settings (default or custom) act like a filter on top of the notification settings configured by your admin. If your admin has turned off a particular notification, you may not receive it even if you’ve chosen to receive that kind of notification in your settings.
Choose email notifications for work item activity in Jira Cloud
Your Jira admin sets up your default notifications. Depending on the space, you may get notifications when someone adds a comment on a work item or someone completes a work log entry. These actions tend to happen in short bursts, with a few small, individual changes added to a work item within minutes of each other.
Instead of sending one email per change, Jira will consolidate individual updates into a single summary email. To make sure relevant updates are batched together, notifications could be delayed by up to 10 minutes.
